Update the `JointStatePublisher` system (`src/systems/joint_state_publisher/JointStatePublisher.cc`) to resolve its `<topic>` using the model namespace when one is set:

new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- LeRobot version: 0.6.1
- Platform: macOS-26.5.2-arm64-arm-64bit
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface Hub version: 1.33.0
- Numpy version: 2.2.6
- PyTorch version: 2.11.0
- Hardware: Koch v1.1 leader, 6x Dynamixel XL330-M077 (firmware v50), 1 Mbps
```

### Description

Calibrating the Koch leader fails at the end with `ValueError: Negative values are not allowed`, because `elbow_flex` is homed to the wrong position.

`koch_leader` puts `elbow_flex` in reverse drive mode (`Drive_Mode = 1`). In that mode the motor reports its position the other way, **homing offset included**, so the offset is subtracted from the position instead of added. `set_half_turn_homings` always assumes `present = actual + offset` for Dynamixel motors. For an inverted motor at reported position `p`, it writes `2047 - p`, and the motor then reads `p - (2047 - p) = 2p - 2047` instead of 2047.

Depending on where the horn sits, the recorded range then goes below 0 and writing `Min_Position_Limit` fails. When it doesn't fail, the calibrated range is silently off-center.

The same logic is still on `main` after the motors refactor: `homing_offset_sign` comes only from the motor definition and ignores the drive mode.

### Context & Reproduction

```bash
lerobot-calibrate --teleop.type=koch_leader --teleop.port=/dev/tty... --teleop.id=my_leader_arm
```
1. Hold the middle pose and press ENTER.
2. Sweep all joints through their range and press ENTER.

After homing, `elbow_flex` should start the sweep at 2047, but its **max** over the whole sweep is 1449, so it was never at 2047.

I confirmed the sign directly on the elbow motor (ID 3, `Drive_Mode = 1`), writing only the `Homing_Offset` register with the arm at rest:

| Homing_Offset | Present_Position |
|---|---|
| 0 | -10 |
| 200 | -210 |
| 0 | -10 |

The offset subtracts from the position it reports.

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell
NAME            |    MIN |    POS |    MAX
shoulder_lift   |   1156 |   3112 |   3136
elbow_flex      |   -728 |    257 |   1449
wrist_flex      |    889 |   1931 |   3045
gripper         |   1684 |   1684 |   2453
INFO 2026-10-22 20:10:42 h_leader.py:178 my_leader_arm KochLeader disconnected.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../lerobot/teleoperators/koch_leader/koch_leader.py", line 130, in calibrate
    self.bus.write_calibration(self.calibration)
  File ".../lerobot/motors/dynamixel/dynamixel.py", line 185, in write_calibration
    self.write("Min_Position_Limit", motor, calibration.range_min)
  ...
  File ".../lerobot/motors/motors_bus.py", line 932, in _serialize_data
    raise ValueError(f"Negative values are not allowed: {value}")
ValueError: Negative values are not allowed: -728
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [ ] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

Probably the same as item 5 of #1489 ("the homing offset on the wrist flex gets set wrong, so half way becomes 0 instead of 2048"), which was closed as stale. #3586 is about a different wrap-around problem.

**Fix:** in `set_half_turn_homings`, negate the offset sign for motors whose `Drive_Mode` has the reverse bit set. I have a PR ready with tests and will link it here.

**Workaround on 0.6.1:** after `set_half_turn_homings`, read back `Present_Position`. For any motor that doesn't read about 2047, write the negated offset. With that, Koch leader calibration completes.

Only tested on XL330-M077 firmware v50. 

I haven't specifically done on Main but the faulty code is there.
new_candidates.title: Koch leader calibration fails with "Negative values are not allowed": homing offset has the wrong sign on motors in reverse drive mode
